entries.title: A US judge clears two brothers accused of stealing $25M in crypto, saying prosecutors failed to prove material misrepresentations in exploiting a software bug (Nate Raymond/Reuters)
Brad Gerstner says Altimeter is aiming to invest $5B in Anthropic's IPO, 5x his largest IPO investment, calling it "a cornerstone compounder for a long time" (Kif Leswing/CNBC)
Customers of BofA, Chase, Wells Fargo, and other US banks report online service issues; Chase says a technical issue, not a cyber issue, is causing delays (Associated Press)
Q&A with Satya Nadella on code verification becoming more important as code generation gets cheap, Microsoft's voluntary exit offers, decision models, and more (Gergely Orosz/The Pragmatic Engineer)
California AG sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face attack, alleging it was one of 80+ incidents resulting from OpenAI testing AI models without adequate safeguards (Politico)
OpenAI announces tools to combat CSAM, including an image classifier and new warning screens to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
Sam Altman says he has "personal strong empathy" for Jensen Huang and "heroes have flaws," but the AI industry "will be fine" due to strong revenues and demand (Shirin Ghaffary/Bloomberg)
Source: Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO and it is focused on a national security investigation into Huang (CNBC)
Anthropic cuts its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, in response to AI-driven bug discovery (Anthropic)
Noeri, which is developing AI software to review and suggest improvements for its clients' AI models and tools, raised $110M led by Menlo Ventures (Dina Bass/Bloomberg)
Harvard study: just 403 US data centers operational between May 2024 and April 2025 consumed as much electricity annually as the state of Michigan (Molly Taft/Wired)
OpenAI says it signed agreements with independent assessors Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire for its first phase of AI model embedded assessments (OpenAI)
Moody's: major US life insurers like Athene held $85.2B in AI debt as of June 30, up 24% from December 31, and the figure could rise to $185B by the end of 2027 (New York Times)
President Trump says he "would not mind" if Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO and "I don't know that she was a spy at all" in reference to Alice Huang (Emily Goodin/New York Post)
Google's TIG reports the first observed instance of attackers using an autonomous AI framework with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits (Duncan Riley/SiliconANGLE)
